item.evidence: frontend/src/lib/zipExport.js:113-114 writes cpp_header || "" and cpp_source || ""; :68-74 renders even an absent setup_guide as a heading; :174-175 does the same for plugin modules. frontend/src/pages/Workspace.jsx:438 only checks result existence, :440 allows issues to be bypassed, :446 builds and :453-454 announces a successful no-code-edits download. backend/projects.py:139-141 accepts an imported system with only system_name.
item.expected: R-217: "If a project's stored C++ or setup content is missing ... shows an error naming the missing part and downloads no partial zip"; R-201 requires an explanation rather than empty files. Missing-content validation should precede packaging, independently of the permission to export compilable-content warnings.
item.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source predicts that a developer importing a legacy/partial system with a name but missing C++ or setup can export an empty, unusable archive. Missing setup alone is not even flagged by checkSystem, which only checks C++. The new catch cannot help because neither builder throws for missing content. The user must inspect the archive and regenerate missing sections; the project itself remains unchanged.
reproduction_steps: Import project JSON containing a named system with missing cpp_source, or a C++ pair but no setup_guide.
Open UE5 .zip and choose Unreal plugin or Source files only.
If prompted, press Export anyway.
Inspect the predicted archive: the absent section is empty/a heading, despite the success toast.
item.surface: Workspace → UE5 .zip → either option; Export anyway
item.title: Exporters receive empty C++ and setup files as a successful ZIP — builders never validate required content

item.evidence: frontend/src/components/CompileCheck.jsx:12-18 renders li/span/div only, with no link, button or handler. frontend/src/pages/Workspace.jsx:112-139 CodeBox accepts no selected-line prop and renders one pre; :819-822 passes no navigation callback between the issue list and either viewer.
item.expected: R-211 (inferred): "choosing the issue highlights that line in the code viewer so the user can find and fix the mistake"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: follow a reference to the content it promises.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: choosing a reported file:line cannot locate or highlight code. Developers can still scroll and count lines manually, so this is small but concrete friction rather than blocked export. This is a source conclusion, not an executed click observation.
reproduction_steps: Open a system with a missing RPC implementation or another line-specific compile issue.
Open C++ Snippets.
Try to activate the issue's .h:line reference with pointer or keyboard.
No code-line selection or navigation is implemented.
item.surface: C++ Snippets → Compile check issue list
item.title: Developers cannot jump from a compile issue to its code line — issues are rendered as inert text

item.evidence: backend/server.py:482-484 validates only that issues is a list; :485-491 filters out all non-dicts and entries lacking a truthy message. Thus {"issues":["missing implementation"]} or {"issues":[{"file":".cpp"}]} becomes {issues:[]}. frontend/src/components/CompileCheck.jsx:80 displays "No further problems found." for that response; Workspace.jsx:571 also receives no AI export warnings.
item.expected: R-194 requires returned issues, a clean message when none are found, or an error; checklist, AI and model features: "Follow parsing, semantic validation ... against the ... field/format ... contract." Malformed issues are not evidence of clean code and must surface a readable-review error rather than a clean verdict.
item.observed: AI and model features: when the provider returns a list containing malformed issue records, the endpoint converts an unreadable review into a successful empty review. A developer is incorrectly reassured the review found no additional problems and can export without those warnings. Actual provider output was not executed; this is the exact source-predicted consequence for those responses. Retrying the review is possible but the UI gives no reason to do so.
reproduction_steps: Press AI review on a C++ pair.
Consider a provider response whose JSON issues array contains a string issue, or an object missing message.
Trace review_cpp: each entry is filtered out and HTTP success returns an empty list.
The panel displays No further problems found and export has no AI issue warning.
item.title: AI review can report a malformed answer as clean — invalid issue entries are silently discarded

item.evidence: frontend/src/lib/zipExport.js:26 recognizes UMG only via /UUserWidget|UMG|WidgetComponent/; the entire DEPS list (:24-38) has no WidgetLayoutLibrary match. :168-172 writes only matched modules plus sibling deps into Build.cs; :174-175 copies the code. Bundle exports use that same writeModule at :260.
item.expected: request: "ready-made Unreal plugin ... so it installs with no code edits"; R-208: "module list ... exactly the set of engine modules the generated code requires, detected from the code's includes and macros". For this witness the independent dependency is UMG, the module that provides Blueprint/WidgetLayoutLibrary.h, regardless of whether code also happens to use UUserWidget.
item.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: a valid stored system that includes Blueprint/WidgetLayoutLibrary.h and calls UWidgetLayoutLibrary::GetViewportScale, with no other UMG-matching symbols, exports with only Core/CoreUObject/Engine dependencies. WidgetLayoutLibrary belongs to UMG, so this otherwise valid UI system cannot compile/link as the advertised drop-in plugin until a developer edits Build.cs. The same failure affects a selected bundle module. This is a source prediction; Unreal compilation was not run.
reproduction_steps: Open/import a system whose valid C++ includes Blueprint/WidgetLayoutLibrary.h and calls UWidgetLayoutLibrary::GetViewportScale, without UUserWidget, UMG or WidgetComponent text.
Export Unreal plugin, or include it alongside another system in Bundle plugin.
Inspect that module's Build.cs: UMG is absent.
Attempt the promised install in a UE5 project without adding dependencies manually; the exported module lacks its required UMG dependency.
item.surface: UE5 .zip → Unreal plugin; Bundle plugin → Download
item.title: Plugin exports using WidgetLayoutLibrary fail to build without edits — dependency detection omits its UMG module

item.evidence: backend/projects.py:214-216 sorts all snapshots by version descending then calls to_list(1000), returning no total/cursor at :217-219. frontend/src/pages/Workspace.jsx:488-489 sets versions to only this reply; :532-533 and frontend/src/components/HistoryModal.jsx:9 list only these versions; restore controls require choosing one (:495-508).
item.expected: R-156: "lists every snapshot newest first"; R-190: "history listing every saved version with its note, saver and time"; request: "roll a project back to any saved version from the Compare menu". Pagination or another reachable continuation must expose the oldest snapshots as well.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: after version 1001 is saved, v1 (and its label/note) is absent from all history and Compare menus even though its snapshot is still stored. An owner/editor cannot discover or restore an important earliest version through the app; viewers also lose its history. Directly constructing a version API request is not an ordinary UI recovery. Source predicts truncation; no thousand-save runtime test was performed.
reproduction_steps: Use a project that has 1001 saved snapshots, naming v1 as an important checkpoint.
Open Compare and History.
Search the named and all-versions groups for v1: the API returns only v1001 through v2.
There is no next-page/load-more control to access or restore v1.
item.title: Older saved versions disappear from Compare and history after 1,000 saves — version listing silently truncates without pagination

item.evidence: backend/projects.py:241-249 updates the project to the restored version before inserting its snapshot with 'Restored from vN'; :250-251 swallows snapshot failure. A concurrent save reads that new project and :185-189 backfills its missing snapshot with snapshot(project), whose default note is empty (:66-70). The unique project/version index is backend/server.py:77. The new corrective note update at projects.py:202-206 covers save_project, not restore_version.
item.expected: R-177: a restore creates a newest version "whose note reads 'Restored from vN'"; R-190 requires the restored version's note in history. The note and snapshot must describe the same committed restore even when a collaborator immediately saves afterward.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: let restore change v2 to v3, then let another editor save before restore's snapshot insert. The save backfills v3 with an empty note and creates v4. Restore's v3 insert then hits the unique index and is silently ignored. The restored contents survive, but the promised 'Restored from vN' history note is permanently lost, leaving the team without the restore's explanation. Ordinary sequential restores work; this finding is the evidenced concurrent interleaving, not a runtime observation.
reproduction_steps: As an editor, restore v1 of a v2 project.
Before restore inserts the v3 snapshot, have a second editor load v3 and save it as v4.
The second save backfills v3 without a note.
Allow restore's snapshot insert to finish: it fails as a duplicate and is ignored; History shows v3 without Restored from v1.
item.surface: Compare → Restore vN; concurrent project Save; Version history
item.title: A restored version can lose its provenance note during a concurrent save — backfill wins the snapshot race and restore swallows the duplicate

item.evidence: frontend/src/lib/compileCheck.js:108 builds defined from function names alone, dropping class identity from defs. :125-127 tests defined.has(`${fn}_Implementation`) without checking which class owns the function. :101 and :114 similarly use one cross-header declaration set for undeclared definitions. headerClasses at zipExport.js:13-15 supports multiple classes, so there is no single-class guard.
item.expected: R-192: the built-in check flags "an undeclared definition, a missing _Implementation function". checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Establish logical record/operation/effect identity"; for C++ methods the identity includes the declaring class, not only the method name. UStamina::Reset_Implementation is not UHealth::Reset_Implementation.
item.observed: Business logic and calculations: for a header declaring UHealth::Reset and UStamina::Reset as BlueprintNativeEvent functions, with only UStamina::Reset_Implementation in the source, the checker considers both functions implemented. Developers miss the expressly supported missing-implementation diagnostic and can receive a clean panel for a pair with UHealth's missing definition. This is a source-predicted false negative, not an executed compiler result. An AI review or compiling outside the app could catch it, but the promised instant local check does not.
reproduction_steps: Import/open a pair whose header has CoreMinimal.h, a final generated include, and two reflected classes UHealth and UStamina, each declaring a BlueprintNativeEvent void Reset().
Include that header in the source and define only UStamina::Reset_Implementation().
Open C++ Snippets.
No missing UHealth::Reset_Implementation issue is added because the global defined set already contains Reset_Implementation.
item.surface: C++ Snippets → built-in Compile check; export warnings
item.title: Missing implementations are hidden when another class has the same method — compile check drops class identity

item.evidence: backend/server.py:48-52 record_usage directly awaits llm_usage.insert_one without handling failure; review_cpp :473 calls it before its provider/error try at :474-480. run_job :346 calls it before send_message inside the same catch as provider failures, and :355 does so before OpenAI streaming. frontend/src/components/CompileCheck.jsx:42-48 maps a failed review request to an error panel.
item.expected: R-206: "a failed usage-counter write does not alter or block the synthesis result"; checklist, Third-party integrations: "Follow unavailable ... dependency outcomes to visible status and recovery." Usage accounting must not prevent otherwise valid provider work, including the newly added review path.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: if the usage insert fails while jobs/project reads and the AI provider are available, review returns an unhandled server error before sending any code to the provider. Synthesis similarly fails before its provider attempt and classifies a database error as an AI-provider error. The developer cannot complete the AI task during that accounting failure even though their key/provider work; retrying is only useful after the accounting problem clears. This is a conditional source prediction, not an observed outage.
reproduction_steps: Use a valid saved AI key and a C++ pair.
Under a failed llm_usage insert (for example a write failure on that collection), press AI review or Synthesize.
record_usage raises before the provider request; review returns a server error and synthesis marks its job failed.
No model request is actually sent, despite the accounting being ancillary.
item.surface: C++ Snippets → AI review; Synthesize; daily usage accounting
item.title: AI review and synthesis fail when usage accounting cannot write — counter insertion is a mandatory unhandled prerequisite

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:647 fixes the left sidebar to w-[320px] shrink-0 and :843 fixes the right to w-[340px] shrink-0, without a narrow-screen replacement. :723 makes the central pane flex-1 min-w-0; its C++ controls live there (:817-824). The header at :587 is a non-wrapping row with all export/save/key buttons (:618-640). frontend/src/App.css:1 fixes the app to 100vw with overflow:hidden; index.css:57-59 also hides document overflow.
item.expected: R-210: at 375px "compile-check panel ... primary controls without overlap or clipping ... export actions remain reachable"; checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "Check containment ... and reachable controls under supported viewports". Fixed sidebars alone require 320+340=660 CSS pixels, exceeding 375 before allocating any center content.
item.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: at a 375px viewport the two unshrinkable sidebars exhaust more than the viewport width, leaving the center pane with no usable width, while the header's export controls overflow a clipped application. A phone user cannot use the central compile-check/review flow or ordinarily reach the top-bar ZIP action; no responsive drawer or horizontal recovery scroll is implemented. Source establishes the width conflict; no browser measurement was performed. A desktop is an alternative device, not a recovery on the affected supported phone.
reproduction_steps: Open a saved project in the workspace at 375 CSS pixels wide.
Try to open C++ Snippets and read/run Compile check or AI review.
Try to reach UE5 .zip in the top header.
The fixed 660px of sidebars and non-wrapping header conflict with the overflow-hidden 375px app; no mobile controls replace them.
item.surface: 375px workspace → C++ Snippets / Compile check / UE5 .zip
item.title: Phone users cannot access compile review or ZIP export — fixed desktop columns and clipped header have no narrow-screen alternative

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:346 captures savingFor and :354 checks it only on success. :363-364 unconditionally closes the dialog and setsConflict for a delayed 409. :1032 loads project.project_id and :1033 calls saveProject(true), both reading the currently open project rather than the project whose request conflicted. Projects remain openable via :718-719 during a save.
item.expected: request's exposed promise: "A slow Save can no longer overwrite a different project you've since opened"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions"; R-068 requires Load/Overwrite to resolve the same project's conflicting save.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: start saving project A, dismiss its still-running save dialog, then open B before A's conflict reply arrives. The new success guard does not guard the error branch, so A's conflict dialog appears over B. Load their version loads B, and Overwrite with mine sends force=true to B instead of A; if B also changed remotely, that bypasses B's ordinary conflict protection. The visible resolution is for the wrong project; a team can overwrite B's collaborator changes under A's warning. This is a source-backed timing prediction. Closing the unexpected dialog is safe, but the offered resolution is not.
reproduction_steps: Have another member save project A so your local base_version is stale.
Press Save on A, then dismiss the Save dialog while its request is delayed.
Open project B from Projects before A's 409 arrives.
Observe the predicted Newer version saved dialog naming A's saver over B; Load their version reloads B and Overwrite with mine forcibly saves B.
item.surface: Save → delayed conflict response → switch project → Newer version saved
item.title: A delayed save conflict offers to overwrite the wrong project — only successful replies check the captured project identity

item.evidence: CompileCheck.jsx:32 keeps result/running state solely in component-local ai; :34 invalidates requests only on a change of system.id, with no unmount cleanup. Workspace.jsx:817 conditionally mounts this component only while tab === 'cpp'. Completion :46 calls onAiIssues even after the old component is unmounted. Parent :571 trusts the last callback for a matching result.id.
item.expected: checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "Resolve ... pending, success ... states against the actual operation state" and preserve context on return; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions". R-212 promises a disabled running review followed by its result, not a fresh idle review while the same operation remains active.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: leaving C++ Snippets during a review and returning unmounts its only running/result state. The button appears idle and can send a second paid/quota-counting review of the same pair while the first still runs. If the newer review completes first, the old unmounted review can subsequently overwrite the parent's export issues for that same system id. Even completed results disappear from the visible panel on an ordinary tab round trip. No provider behavior was observed; this follows from component ownership and callbacks. Users can avoid the problem by not navigating during/after review, but that is not the supported tab interaction.
reproduction_steps: Start AI review on a C++ system.
Switch to Setup Guide, then back to C++ Snippets before it finishes.
The newly mounted panel has an enabled AI review button; press it to start another request.
Let the second response finish before the first: the old callback can replace export warnings with the older response, and navigating again clears the panel's visible review.
item.surface: C++ Snippets → AI review → another tab → C++ Snippets; export warnings
item.title: Tab navigation loses the running AI review and allows competing results — review state and invalidation belong to an unmounted tab

item.evidence: Modal.jsx:5-9 registers only Escape handling; :11-18 uses aria-modal but sets no initial focus, focus trap, inert background or restoration. BundleModal.jsx:55 has no autofocus; Workspace.jsx:987-1003 autofocuses the note field but does not isolate background controls. The page and background controls remain mounted and focusable behind the fixed backdrop.
item.expected: checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "keyboard focus ... follows the active surface" and "Dialog close ... restores ... focus"; "an editor overlay must preserve the supported focus/background interaction contract." R-210 includes usable save/history/bundle dialogs. Aria-modal must correspond to actual keyboard isolation.
item.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: opening Bundle or History leaves focus on the covered trigger, and tabbing through Save can leave its dialog for still-active workspace controls. Keyboard users can focus/activate controls behind the modal rather than the visible dialog, including project navigation; no focus is restored to the initiating control on close. Pointer backdrop handling does not prevent this. The user can cycle focus manually or close the dialog, so the demonstrated impact is recoverable accessibility/interaction impairment, not an asserted total keyboard lockout. No browser focus test was executed.
reproduction_steps: Use the keyboard to open Bundle plugin or History.
Press Tab repeatedly: no handler confines focus to the dialog, and initial focus was never moved into it.
Open Save and tab beyond its Cancel/Save buttons; background controls remain in the tab order.
Close the dialog and note there is no source path restoring focus to its trigger.
item.surface: Bundle plugin, Save, History and export-check modals
item.title: Keyboard focus escapes new dialogs into covered project controls — shared modal implements no focus isolation or restoration

item.evidence: CompileCheck.jsx:44 sends every local issue with known_issues: issues.map(issueText), without a cap. backend/server.py:457 restricts known_issues to max_length=40; FastAPI rejects the body before review_cpp executes. compileCheck.js:119-127 adds one error per missing UFUNCTION implementation, with no total issue bound.
item.expected: R-194: "An 'AI review' button beside the compile check calls the review endpoint ... then renders the returned issues ... or a plain-English error"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Compare request/response contracts at both ends ... fields, types". A supported code pair should remain reviewable when its built-in issue count exceeds the context limit; send only the supported known-issues context or otherwise reconcile the boundary.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: a short header with 41 declared but unimplemented BlueprintCallable functions generates 41 local issues, then AI review always receives 422 instead of reaching the model. This is especially likely when a broken generation leaves many functions unimplemented, precisely when review is needed. The UI renders a validation message but offers no way to reduce the known-issues array because code is read-only; the developer must regenerate or edit/reimport the code before reviewing. This is a bounded review failure, not a provider observation.
reproduction_steps: Open/import a C++ pair with the normal includes/reflected class and 41 unimplemented UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable) declarations in its header.
Open C++ Snippets and ensure an AI key is saved.
Press AI review.
The client posts at least 41 known_issues; the endpoint contract rejects it before any AI review occurs.
item.title: Developers cannot AI-review code with more than 40 local issues — client sends an array the endpoint rejects

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:227-235 decides to warn only from the cached useUsage result. UsageChip.jsx:12-20 fetches usage only when aiKey or refreshKey changes, not on synthesis preflight or other-tab calls; :25-27 turns missing usage into used=0/limit=null. server.py:393-400 resolves headers then unconditionally creates the job; GenerateRequest :104-123 has no confirm_limit field or server usage check.
item.expected: request: "Warn before a synthesis when you're close to today's free Gemini limit"; R-182: "nothing is sent until a choice is made"; R-183 requires the high-usage server warning before a job starts. For the concrete supported witness, 450 / 500 = 90%, unambiguously above the stated approximately 85% warning threshold.
item.observed: Business logic and calculations: leave tab B open after it fetched a low count, then consume 450 of the key's 500 estimated requests in tab A. Tab B still sees its old low count and starts a new synthesis without warning or confirmation; the server also never checks authoritative usage. The same bypass occurs while the initial usage fetch is pending. Users lose the promised advance notice and can unexpectedly spend their remaining quota. Source predicts this stale-tab lifecycle; no provider quota was consumed in review. Reloading first is possible but undiscoverable because B displays an apparently current daily count.
reproduction_steps: Open two tabs with the same Gemini key/model while today's usage is low.
In tab A, bring today's app-recorded usage to 450 of the model's estimated 500 requests.
Without reloading tab B, press Synthesize there.
Tab B uses its cached low usage and the backend starts a job without limit_warning or confirmation.
item.surface: Synthesize in a stale or newly opened tab; POST /api/generate
item.title: Near-limit users can synthesize without any quota warning — cached client usage is never rechecked before the server starts work

item.evidence: PublicView.jsx:46 awaits buildPluginZip and then downloads, with no try/catch or error state. Workspace.jsx:445-449 now catches the same builder failure and shows Couldn't build the zip. zipExport.js:210-213 calls setupMd; :70 calls (system.setup_guide || []).forEach without shape validation. projects.py:139-141,160-168 accept named imported systems without validating setup_guide's type.
item.expected: R-217: "if ... the zip build throws, the export action shows an error ... downloads no partial zip"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "visible rejected/skipped input"; R-218 exposes the same plugin export to share-link readers. Failure feedback must cover this consumer as well as the owner's workspace.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: a share-link reader's plugin export fails silently when the builder rejects, unlike the corrected workspace path. For a concrete reachable input, import an otherwise usable named system with setup_guide stored as a nonempty string, save and share it; setupMd throws because forEach is not a function. The public button's async rejection is unhandled and the page gives no explanation or recovery. The owner can repair/reimport the project, but the reader cannot; no data is changed and no runtime download was attempted during review.
reproduction_steps: Import/save a project with C++ content and a nonempty string instead of an array for setup_guide; the importer currently accepts it.
Enable its public link and open the /share/<token> page.
Press Unreal plugin .zip.
The builder throws during setup markdown creation; the share page implements no error message for this failure.
item.title: Share-link readers get no explanation when ZIP creation fails — public export omits the workspace's new error handling
